_comment: InSight — registered as a platform service.
Three entries and one wire. The Bicep module provisions ~20 Azure resources
behind Private Link and emits a single `appInfra` OBJECT; that object is
wired onto the chart's `.Values.appInfra`, which is the whole contract
between them. Everything else the chart needs it derives from that.
Credentials never appear here. The tenant supplies four to the secret store;
they land in the tenant's own Key Vault, the module reads them from there
with Key Vault references (never as parameters), and the chart's own
ExternalSecrets read the six contract secrets the module writes — using the
workload identity the module federated. So the value goes tenant -> vault ->
pod without passing through the catalog, the control plane, or the template.
Depends on external-secrets: the chart ships its own SecretStore and
ExternalSecret resources, which do nothing without that controller.
IMAGES: the nine first-party insight images are not reachable from this
environment — see NOTES.md. imageRegistry below points at the platform
registry; replace it with the real one when access exists.

secretSets.name: insight secrets
secretSets.description: Credentials InSight needs. Supplied once by each tenant: they provision the database and are read by the app at runtime. Stored in the tenant's own Key Vault, where the platform cannot read them back.

infrastructure.name: insight infra
infrastructure.description: InSight's Azure footprint: Key Vault with customer-managed keys, Postgres, Redis, Service Bus, Storage, AI Search, three Cognitive accounts and App Configuration — all reachable only over Private Link — plus the workload identity and federated credentials its pods authenticate with.

applications.name: insight
applications.description: InSight admin portal — a ten-service application. Reads every credential from the tenant's own Key Vault at runtime via workload identity.
